description: Role catalog for the seeded fleet. A scenario names a fixture ROLE; the runner (hack/fleet-kubeconfigs.sh) discovers the leased project's seeded clusters by label, matches each to a slot below, confirms every object in the role's `probes` list is present, and only then writes that role's kubeconfig. Nothing outside this file may address a seeded cluster or an eval project directly: each project carries its own trio, so a case written against one must run unchanged against all of them. Names, prefix and location are deliberately absent -- they are the Terraform's business and are read back off the discovered clusters. See README.md, 'Addressing a fixture by role'. One sanctioned exception: hack/ci-eval-pr.sh section 3b discovers the slot-c cluster by these same labels and reuses it as the gpu-stress-test log-fixture subject -- it mutates nothing in-cluster, writes only project-level Cloud Logging entries that name the cluster, and falls back to a per-run cluster when slot c is absent, not RUNNING, or its default namespace is not empty.
probe_syntax: Each probe is `<kind>/<name>` or `<kind>?<label-selector>`, read against the role's `namespace` when it has one. A role's namespace is probed implicitly. A probe is the runner's promise that the object was THERE before the agent ran, and it is the only thing that entitles a check to call the same object's later absence a violation rather than an environment that was never ready -- so every subject a task.yaml asserts on must appear here, which bench/tests/test_fleet_verifier.py enforces in both directions. A role with an empty list confirms nothing, and its checks can never blame the run for an absence.

cluster_slots.a: Every namespace-level defect, plus the idle and pinned node pools.
cluster_slots.b: Control plane held one minor behind the REGULAR channel default.
cluster_slots.c: The consistency outlier: no master authorized networks.

crashloop-workload.fixture: payments-api Deployment, deterministic OOMKilled crashloop, 64Mi memory limit

no-pdb-workload.fixture: checkout-gateway Deployment, two replicas, no PodDisruptionBudget in the namespace

hpa-saturated.fixture: inference-server HPA settles above pinned-inference-pool's capped capacity, leaving Pending replicas. Both halves are probed: the HPA declares the gap and cluster-agent-pending-replicas-capped-pool additionally asserts the Deployment's nodeSelector and CPU request, the two fields that would make the Pending replicas schedulable

rbac-overgrant.fixture: debug-binding ClusterRoleBinding granting cluster-admin to the seeded-security default ServiceAccount

idle-nodepool.fixture: idle-batch-pool node pool running zero non-system pods, held empty by a NO_SCHEDULE taint

version-laggard.fixture: control plane one minor behind the REGULAR channel default, held by a NO_MINOR_UPGRADES exclusion

drift-outlier.fixture: master authorized networks absent where both cohort peers have it on
